newsitem.title: UK: Britain's SFA settles with former Barings exec Walz.
newsitem.headline: Britain's SFA settles with former Barings exec Walz.

text.p: Britain's Securities and Futures Authority (SFA), the financial markets regulator, said on Tuesday the disciplinary proceedings it had brought against former Barings executive Mary Walz had been settled.

But the regulator gave no details of the agreement. "Until a board notice and further press release is issued, SFA and Ms Walz have agreed not to comment on the terms of the settlement," the SFA said in a statement.
Britain's SFA settles with former Barings exec Walz

Last week Walz, a former boss of rogue trader Nick Leeson, lost a claim for a 500,000 pound ($821,400) bonus against ING Barings, the investment bank formed when Dutch financial group Internationale Nederlanden Groep took over Barings when it collapsed under huge losses in February 1995.

Walz, who was equity derivatives head at Barings' investment banking arm, was among those dismissed by ING when it took over the blue-blooded bank after Singapore-based Leeson rang up losses of nearly $1.4 billion in unauthorised trading.
The SFA has already banned several former Barings employees including Peter Norris, chief executive of the failed bank, from working in the City.

But last month an independent tribunal cleared another former Barings executive, who had challenged the SFA, of most misconduct charges. Following the settlement of the Walz proceedings, the SFA now has two outstanding cases against former Barings bosses to complete. ($1=.6087 Pound)
